extracted.intended_audience: students, critics, and reformers of democratic politics; educated general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Normative guidance on the role of critics, exceptional individuals, and social reform in achieving a mature democratic order; prescriptive political theory about how democracy should be cultivated and evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of a critic in a democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental duty of a critic in a democracy is to see that the results of these experiences are not misinterpreted and that the best interpretation is embodied in popular doctrinal form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critic is consequently not so much the guide as the lantern which illuminates the path. He may not pretend to know the only way or all the ways; but he should know as much as can be known about the traveled road.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critic's epistemic humility and practical knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A critic should not claim to know the only way or all the ways; instead he should know as much as can be known about the traveled road.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes practical familiarity with experience over ideological certainty; the critic illuminates rather than dictates, ensuring popular doctrine reflects best interpretations of experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of exceptional moral individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Men endowed with high moral gifts and capable of exceptional moral achievements have their special part to play in the building of an enduring democratic structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although their importance may be under-estimated, such figures (e.g., Abraham Lincoln) who combine specific efficiency with kindliness become national exemplars whose lives have consummate value for democratic culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral feeling is not a substitute for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A profound sense of human brotherhood is no substitute for specific efficiency; consummate faith itself is no substitute for good work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against relying solely on benevolent sentiment (Tolstoyan error); effective democratic improvement requires concrete, competent action as well as moral feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social reorganization and individual emancipation as prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Back of any work of moral conversion must come a long and slow process of social reorganization and individual emancipation; and not until the reorganization has been partly accomplished, and the individual released, disciplined and purified, will the soil be prepared for the crowning work of some democratic Saint Francis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places priority on structural and personal transformation before expecting mass moral conversion; implies policy and institutional work are indispensable preconditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic fulfillment requires conscious, laborious work
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention has been concentrated on that indispensable phase of the work which can be attained by conscious means. Until this work is measurably accomplished no evangelist can do more than convert a few men for a few years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between limited spiritual leadership and broad democratic reform; large-scale improvement depends on deliberate, sustained reforms rather than charismatic conversion alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass enthusiasm must be rooted in achieved experience and tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: The laborious work of individual and social fulfillment may eventually be transfigured by an outburst of enthusiasm—one which is not the expression of a mood, but which is substantially the finer flower of an achieved experience and a living tradition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any transformative popular enthusiasm is legitimate and stable only if it grows out of real accomplishments and a living tradition, not ephemeral moods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy entails an aspiration toward human perfectibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For better or worse, democracy cannot be disentangled from an aspiration toward human perfectibility, and hence from the adoption of measures looking in the direction of realizing such an aspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies that democratic policy should include measures aimed at moral and personal improvement of citizens; such measures are part of democratic coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation of exemplary leaders as means of civic improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The common citizen can become something of a saint and something of a hero, not by growing to heroic proportions in his own person, but by the sincere and enthusiastic imitation of heroes and saints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extent to which citizens adopt higher moral standards depends on the ability of exceptional fellow-countrymen to offer acceptable examples of heroism and saintliness; role-modeling is thus a practical tool of civic formation.
